qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: GEICO shares low-cost direct distribution scale with drivers, BNSF operates an irreplaceable transcontinental rail duopoly, and Berkshire Hathaway Reinsurance exploits an unreplicable balance sheet fortress to price hard-market risks. 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 16.7% and operating ROIC of 19.6% confirm durable competitive advantage despite ASU 2016-01 mark-to-market net income volatility.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Unrivaled conglomerate engine anchored by negative-cost insurance float ($170B+), scale economies shared at GEICO, an irreplaceable transcontinental freight rail duopoly at BNSF, and essential regulated utility infrastructure at BHE. Structurally insulated from AI disruption, highly resilient to inflation, and a major beneficiary of US industrial supply-chain reshoring. Unassailable fortress balance sheet holding >$350B in liquid sovereign Treasury bills providing unmatched dry powder and resilience. Seamless succession to CEO Greg Abel and insurance head Ajit Jain preserves cultural and capital allocation excellence. [5-10Y g: operating earnings volume 3.5% + tariff/underwriting price 2.0% + float deployment & T-bill yield 1.5% - capex excess over D&A 0.5% + opportunistic share repurchases 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: Reported 10-year financials demonstrate exceptional operating compounding: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 16.69% and Operating ROIC of 19.64%. FY2025 operating earnings were $44.5B (following $47.4B in FY2024), driven by robust insurance underwriting recovery and steady utility/rail volumes. Segment profile spans critical infrastructure and non-discretionary Western commerce: Insurance (GEICO, Berkshire Hathaway Reinsurance Group, General Re) holding >$170B of zero/negative-cost float; Freight Rail (BNSF, 32,500 route miles transporting essential freight); Energy (BHE, 5.3M customers and massive renewable/transmission asset base); and industrial manufacturing (Precision Castparts, Marmon, Lubrizol, McLane). OCF was $45.97B in FY2025 and $49.20B in FY2023; the lower screening FCF conversion (0.44) is entirely an accounting distortion of ASU 2016-01 unrealized mark-to-market gains in GAAP net income rather than cash flow leakage. Balance sheet holds >$350B in cash and short-term US Treasury bills with zero net debt at the holding parent (subsidiary debt at BHE/BNSF is non-recourse). Capital allocation history is the global gold standard under Warren Buffett, now successfully transitioned to CEO Greg Abel and non-executive Chairman Howard Buffett.
